spec.title: Campaign 2 (the initiative system) — CLOSE report
spec.p: _2026-07-10 16:40. The campaign-close narrative per the reports law. Normative: the plan's §2 execution record + §14 ledger + §15 deferrals; MT-C2-01…04. Campaign commits: `47412ad` → the close pair, 19 total (15 planned, ≤ 26 budget — P7 green)._

section.title: What was done, end to end
section.p: One day, two sessions, seven phases. The campaign built the entire initiative loop: boss sessions + run attribution in MC (`FRACTALITY_BOSS_SESSION` via CLAUDE_ENV_FILE), the pure `fractality-initiative` engine (scoreboard render, nudge policy, route calculus — strictly factual by D7), seven new CLI verbs (`session scoreboard route hook statusline harness fetch`), the CC adapter under the availability law (any failure → silent exit 0), threshold nudges with cooldown, stop-time parked-question pushes with folded acks, profile auto-answer rules, the matrix as embedded data with 10/10 goldens — and then measured the whole thing against six cold GLM bosses in a pre-registered A/B trial.

section.title: The verdicts
section.p: Seven of eight predictions held; the falsified one is the campaign's most instructive result (full channel analysis in the Ф6 report and MT-C2-04): the nudge channel is structurally silent in single-prompt `-p` sessions (F23), a fresh home shows an empty — hence unpersuasive — scoreboard (F25), and a broken staging toolchain let every boss rationally doubt worker self-verification (F24, shared by both arms).

list.item: **Honesty over the bet.** The falsification is recorded verbatim; no post-hoc threshold tuning, no metric surgery. The trial's pre-registration proved its worth the first time it was inconvenient.

**The levers become mandate seeds, not patches** — DEF-C2-1 (a mid-work injection seam that exists in headless sessions), DEF-C2-2 (worker-credibility facts on the boss surface + a fixed staging toolchain), DEF-C2-3 (the cold-board problem), DEF-C2-4 (re-run design: multi-prompt, N>3, Opus-class boss when budget allows).

**RP2 recommendation stands on data:** post-tool-use counter default-ON (P95 51 ms, half the budget). RP3 (settings target) keeps the `.claude/settings.local.json` recommendation. Both remain owner-open.

**The adapter is production-shaped:** across six hostile-cold runs, hooks installed/fired/exited-0 flawlessly, sessions attributed, counters counted, and no boss session was ever broken — the availability law is field-proven.
**Owner sign-off** on MT-C2-01…04 (pre-run records are in; the pass is the owner's — manual-tests law).
**Staging toolchain defect** (F24) — fix before any re-run (DEF-C2-2a).

Standing leftovers, now in §15: hook debug channel (failures are silent by law — good for bosses, blind for developers), session TTL reaping, per-packet answer rules, `auto_answered` in stats, quota ceilings.

The cwd law claimed its second boss-side strike (a floor launched from the host root; caught by specmap, relaunched pinned). The law needs mechanical enforcement someday — a shell-side guard, not memory.

The product thesis is intact but sharpened: **the fabric works; the persuasion layer is unproven in headless mode and untested in interactive mode.** Interactive sessions (statusline alive, multi-prompt nudges real) are where Campaign 2's bet gets its fair fight — that's the follow-up's arena (DEF-C2-1/-4).

The delegation matrix cuts both ways: a fluent model quotes it back to justify keeping work. The next surface iteration should encode the *pro-delegation counter-arguments* (verification economics, parallelism wins) as data the boss can cite, not just guardrails it can weaponize.

Session delegation scoreboard (the law's enforcement line): **delegated 6** — the six trial boss-runs themselves (GLM did all eight menu tasks six times over; that WAS the experiment); **kept with cause** — scoring (frozen-protocol interpretation), the two 20-iteration benches (smaller than a packet round-trip), and all close authoring (plan/report/WAL — the never-delegate set). No violation to record.
